title: Complexity of Littlewood-Richardson Coefficients
description: Decidable LR coefficient computation for 2-row partitions with verified Gr(2,4) structure constants, multiplicity-free property, and complexity dichotomy (positivity in P vs counting #P-complete).

meta.author: Lean Genius Research
meta.assumptions: axiomCount = 3 reflects three complexity-theoretic theorems (lr_saturation_theorem, lr_positivity_in_P, lr_counting_sharp_P_complete) that assert `True` as explicit placeholders rather than proving their named statements — the complexity theory formalism is not available in Lean/Mathlib, so these are unproven assumptions (no `axiom` declarations appear in the source, but per the Axiom Integrity Policy these placeholder assertions are counted as assumptions). The 2-row LR coefficient computation (lrCoeff2) and full Gr(2,4) multiplication table are fully verified via native_decide; the entry is not status `verified` because the headline complexity results are not formally proved.

overview.historicalContext: Littlewood-Richardson coefficients c^nu_{lam,mu} are fundamental in algebraic combinatorics, governing the multiplication of Schur functions, tensor product decomposition of GL_n representations, and Schubert calculus on Grassmannians. The Knutson-Tao saturation theorem (1999) showed that testing positivity (c > 0) reduces to linear programming, placing it in P. Narayanan (2006) proved that exact computation of these coefficients is #P-complete, establishing one of the sharpest complexity separations in combinatorics.
overview.problemStatement: Formalize a concrete, decidable computation of LR coefficients for 2-row partitions. Verify the multiplication table of the Chow ring A*(Gr(2,4)). Document the P vs #P complexity dichotomy.
overview.proofStrategy: For 2-row partitions, an LR tableau is parameterized by k1 = number of 1s in row 1. The valid range of k1 is determined by four conditions: row capacity, column strictly-increasing, and the ballot/lattice-word condition. All conditions are decidable and checked via Finset.filter. Verification uses native_decide to evaluate lrCoeff2 on all 216 triples of Gr(2,4) Schubert classes.
keyInsights: For 2-row SSYT, a filling is uniquely parameterized by k1 (1s in row 1), making the counting problem 1-dimensional
The nontrivial zero sigma_2 * sigma_11 = 0 arises from conflicting constraints: column condition forces k2 = 0 but range forces k2 >= 1
Gr(2,4) is multiplicity-free: all LR coefficients in {0,1}, verified by native_decide over 216 triples
The P vs #P gap for LR coefficients is one of the sharpest complexity separations in combinatorics

Commutativity c^ν_{λ,μ} = c^ν_{μ,λ} is proved directly from the algorithmic definition by showing the five deciding conditions are symmetric under λ ↔ μ; the Pieri converse shows that c^ν_{(k,0),μ} = 1 characterizes exactly the horizontal strips

conclusion.summary: This file provides a fully verified, decidable computation of Littlewood-Richardson coefficients for 2-row partitions, confirming all structure constants of the Chow ring A*(Gr(2,4)) and establishing the general multiplicity-free property for all Gr(2,n) via a structural proof that requires no enumeration.
conclusion.implications: The formalization demonstrates that the LR rule — while #P-complete in general — reduces to constant-time computation for the 2-row case: at most five decidable comparisons determine any coefficient. The Pieri formula, commutativity, and the full Gr(2,4) multiplication table are verified machine-checked theorems. The sharp P vs #P complexity dichotomy is documented with precise references to Knutson-Tao (1999) and Narayanan (2006), making this entry a self-contained reference for the computational complexity of Schubert calculus.
openQuestions: Can the decidable 2-row LR computation be extended to 3-row partitions in Lean, and can Narayanan's #P-hardness reduction be formally verified once complexity theory is available in Mathlib?
Is there a Lean formalization of the Knutson-Tao honeycomb model that would upgrade lr_saturation_theorem from a vacuous placeholder to a genuine machine-checked theorem?
What is the minimal Mathlib extension needed to formally state and prove that LR positivity reduces to a polynomial-time linear program via Klyachko's horn inequalities?

sections.title: Part I: 2-Row Partitions
sections.summary: Partition2 structure (a >= b >= 0) with DecidableEq/Repr, size, and decidable containment.

sections.title: Part II: LR Coefficient for 2-Row Partitions
sections.summary: Decidable lrCoeff2 via the standard reverse row reading word (Fulton convention); ballot condition forces row 1 all-ones, so the result is always 0 or 1.

sections.title: Part III: Verified Values for Gr(2,4)
sections.summary: All 7 nonzero structure constants of A*(Gr(2,4)) verified, plus the nontrivial zero c^{(2,2)}_{(2,0),(1,1)}=0 and universal size-mismatch and non-containment zero theorems.

sections.title: Part IV: Gr(2,4) Multiplicity-Free Property
sections.summary: All 6^3 = 216 LR coefficients among the 6 Gr(2,4) Schubert classes lie in {0,1}; full multiplication table proved explicitly by native_decide.

sections.title: Part V: General Structural Properties
sections.summary: General multiplicity-free theorem lrCoeff2_le_one for all Gr(2,n), the identity c^lambda_{lambda,0}=1, and regression tests against the old (incorrect) reading-word definition.

sections.title: Part VI: Decidability of LR Coefficients
sections.summary: LR coefficient equality and positivity are decidable instances; the 2-row case is computable in O(1) comparisons (constant-time, in P).

sections.title: Part VII: Complexity Results (Documentation)
sections.summary: Knutson-Tao saturation, P-membership of positivity, and #P-completeness of counting (Narayanan 2006) recorded as theorems with vacuous formal content (True) -- no axioms.

sections.title: Part VIII: The Complexity Gap as a Mathematical Phenomenon
sections.summary: Concrete witnesses that LR values depend on partition shape, not size alone: c^{(2,2)}_{(2,0),(1,1)}=0 vs c^{(2,2)}_{(1,1),(1,1)}=1, illustrating the positivity/counting hardness gap.

sections.title: Part IX: Symmetry and Pieri Formula
sections.summary: Right identity, commutativity lrCoeff2_comm (c^nu_{lambda,mu}=c^nu_{mu,lambda}), and the Pieri formula with converse: c^nu_{(k,0),mu}=1 iff nu/mu is a horizontal strip of size k.

sections.title: Summary
sections.summary: Recap: concrete lrCoeff2 definition, Gr(2,4) verification, general multiplicity-free, two-sided identity, commutativity, Pieri formula, 0 axioms, and the complexity dichotomy.

mainTheorems.name: gr24_multiplicity_free
mainTheorems.description: All Gr(2,4) LR coefficients are 0 or 1 (multiplicity-free)
mainTheorems.leanType: ∀ ν ∈ gr24_classes, ∀ λ ∈ gr24_classes, ∀ μ ∈ gr24_classes, lrCoeff2 ν λ μ ≤ 1

mainTheorems.name: lr_sigma2_sigma11_zero
mainTheorems.description: The nontrivial zero: sigma_2 * sigma_11 = 0 in A*(Gr(2,4))

mainTheorems.name: lr_value_depends_on_shape
mainTheorems.description: LR coefficient depends on partition shape, not just size
mainTheorems.leanType: ∃ ν λ₁ λ₂ μ, λ₁.size = λ₂.size ∧ lrCoeff2 ν λ₁ μ ≠ lrCoeff2 ν λ₂ μ
